notes.children: A `children` map's entries are EITHER a bare childTaskId string (childIndex = its array position) OR an explicit { childTaskId, childIndex } object. The object form exists to put childIndex DELIBERATELY out of array order, which is the only way to observe that both applyMemberRules and planDerivedTasks sort children by childIndex before using them.
notes.sourceWindows: `sourceWindows` values are bare timeframe strings; the harness wraps each into a BoardWindow with startDate = null and endDate = null before passing it as `sourceWindowByTaskId`. Swift must wrap identically or CUSTOM handling will diverge.
notes.sourceWindowByTaskId: Keyed by every id whose source window matters - supplied members AND the children of a One-square compound. A compound's parts are pro-rated by looking up the CHILD's id (e.g. c1), never the compound's (C), so sourceWindows deliberately carries NO entry for C or C2: an implementation that keys the lookup by the compound id gets null source days, skips pro-rating and fails the One-square auto vectors.

windowDays.name: custom 10-day span inclusive
windowDays.note: UTC day numbers differ by 9; inclusive span = 9 + 1 = 10.

windowDays.name: custom across DST end (US) still calendar days
windowDays.note: Only the YYYY-MM-DD prefix is read, so the extra local hour on 2026-11-01 is invisible: Oct 30 -> Nov 2 is 3 UTC days, + 1 = 4.

autoTarget.name: tiny goal floors at 1 via ceil: ceil(1x1/30)=1

varyRange.name: level 2 +/-50% of 10, hi clamped to goal 12 then [5,12]
lo clamps at 1: t=1 lvl2 then [max(1,round(0.5))=1, round(1.5)=2]
t above goal is clamped first: t=50 goal=20 lvl1 then [16,20]
half-up tie: t=3 lvl2 then [round(1.5)=2, round(4.5)=5]
varyRange.note: Pins the rounding convention as HALF-UP (away from zero), not half-to-even: banker's rounding would give [2,4]. Swift's default .rounded() is .toNearestOrAwayFromZero, which matches - do not substitute .toNearestOrEven.

varyRange.name: half-up tie: t=5 lvl2 then [round(2.5)=3, round(7.5)=8]
varyRange.note: The lo half of the same convention: half-to-even would give lo = 2.

rollTarget.name: level 0 never calls rng (rng that throws)
t above goal, level 0 then clamped goal

vectors.name: no rules then identity, empty partOf
split with one excluded part
last-part guard: all excluded then all contribute
stale rule for a task not in supply is skipped
stale part rule (c9) skipped; split still expands
split on a non-compound member then member stays
split on a childless compound then member stays
One-square (split false) is not expanded
split expands in childIndex order, not array order
vectors.note: E's children are stored [c3 (childIndex 1), c1 (childIndex 0)], so array order would give [c3, c1]. The sort by childIndex is what makes the expansion deterministic across platforms.

vectors.name: duplicate childIndex breaks the tie on childTaskId, not insertion order
vectors.note: F's children are stored [c3, c1] and BOTH carry childIndex 0. A comparator on childIndex alone is not total: TS's stable sort would keep insertion order ([c3, c1]) while Swift's unstable `sorted` may not, so the two platforms could expand the same compound in different orders. The comparator is (childIndex, childTaskId), so the tie resolves to [c1, c3] on both.

vectors.name: board counting auto (recurring): r1 35 weekly to daily gives 5; baseline 12
board counting override: target 20 wins over auto
board counting oneOff, no target then goal (no auto)
vary roll on board auto: t=5 lvl1 then [4,6]; seed 42 gives 4+floor(0.2523x3)=4
pool counting as-is (no vary)
vectors.note: ANY target on a pool source is ignored - member-level (here) or part-level (see the split-part and One-square pool vectors below). A pool member offers vary / split / part-exclusion and nothing else, so this member is placed as-is.

vectors.name: pool counting with vary: t=goal=10 lvl2 then [5,10]; seed 42 gives 5+floor(0.2523x6)=6
hand-added with manualTaskVary: r2 lvl1 then [8,10]; seed 42 gives 8; baseline 3
vectors.note: r2 goal is 10 and a hand-added member rolls around its own goal, so varyRange(10,1,10) = [max(1,round(8))=8, min(10,round(12)=12)=10] = [8,10] (hi clamps to the goal). sample1 = 1083814273/2^32 = 0.25235, so 8 + floor(0.25235 x 3) = 8 + 0 = 8. Corrected from the brief's 9, which used the rollTarget vector's unclamped [8,12] range (goal 20) instead of r2's goal of 10.

vectors.name: hand-added counting without vary then as-is; normal always as-is
hand-added wins over source copy: r1 in a board supply AND manual, no manual vary then as-is
split part on a board source: c1 8 weekly to daily gives ceil(8/7)=2; part target 3 overrides to 3
split part auto (no part target): c1 then 2
vectors.note: member-level vary is IGNORED in split mode: the part carries no vary of its own, so t=autoTarget(8,7,1)=2 at lvl0 gives 2 and the rng is untouched.

vectors.name: One-square compound with member-level vary on a board source then derived compound; c1 auto 2, lvl1 gives [round(1.6)=2, round(2.4)=2] = 2; c2 original
vectors.note: lo == hi so the roll short-circuits and never samples the rng.

vectors.name: One-square compound with a part target only: board source, parts.c1.target 4 then derived compound, c1 gives 4
vectors.note: A part-level target is honoured on BOARD sources only, so this vector uses kind board. The explicit 4 beats autoTarget(8,7,1)=2; vary is 0 so the rng is untouched.

vectors.name: One-square compound with no rule on a board source then as-is
window-stamped hand-added member re-mints: w1 (root r1, maxCount 5) then derived root r1, target 5, baseline 12
supplying-source precedence: first source in order wins (pool first then as-is even though a later board source also lists r1)
two rolls consume rng in selectedIds order: r1 (board auto 5, lvl1 [4,6]) then r2 (pool lvl1 [8,10])
vectors.note: sample1 = 1083814273/2^32 = 0.25235 so r1 = 4 + floor(0.25235 x 3) = 4. sample2 = 378494188/2^32 = 0.08813 so r2 = 8 + floor(0.08813 x 3) = 8. The brief wrote r2's range as [8,12] and multiplied by 5; r2's goal is 10 so the range is [8,10] (3 values) - the result is 8 either way.

vectors.name: third sample never taken: three level-1 rolls r1 [4,6], r2 [8,10], c1 (board auto 2 then [2,2] lo==hi so NO sample)
vectors.note: sample3 = 2479403867/2^32 = 0.57728 is left unconsumed - asserted via a counting rng wrapper (expectedRngCalls = 2). As in the two-roll vector, r2's range is [8,10] not the brief's [8,12]; the result 8 is unchanged.

vectors.name: split part with a target on a pool source then placed as-is
vectors.note: The part-level twin of the member-level pool vector: target 5 is ignored because the source is a pool, and with no vary there is nothing left to derive, so c1 is placed as its original self. Contrast the board-source split vector, where the same part target yields a derived counter.

vectors.name: children roll in childIndex order, not array order
vectors.note: C2's children are stored [c1 (childIndex 1), c3 (childIndex 0)], so childIndex order is c3 then c1 - the reverse of array order. c3 (childIndex 0) first: target 10 vary 1, goal 20, varyRange(10,1,20) = [max(1,round(8))=8, min(20,round(12)=12)=12] = [8,12]; sample1 = 1083814273/2^32 = 0.25235, 8 + floor(0.25235 x 5 = 1.2617) = 9. c1 (childIndex 1) second: target 6 vary 2, goal 8, varyRange(6,2,8) = [max(1,round(3))=3, min(8,round(9)=9)=8] = [3,8]; sample2 = 378494188/2^32 = 0.08813, 3 + floor(0.08813 x 6 = 0.5288) = 3. Array order would instead give c1 = 3+floor(0.25235x6=1.514) = 4 and c3 = 8+floor(0.08813x5=0.441) = 8, so this vector discriminates. Both parts derive, so expectedRngCalls is 2.

vectors.name: One-square compound with a part target on a pool source then as-is
vectors.note: The One-square twin of the split-part pool vector, and the pool counterpart of the board vector directly above: a part-level target is ignored on a pool source, so no part derives, the whole compound is placed as its original self, and the rng is untouched. This is also the only vector that reaches the "a rule exists but derives nothing" exit (as opposed to the no-rule-at-all exit).

vectors.name: action-less counting member keeps its own title
vectors.note: a1 has no action and no unit, so the derived draft carries action = "" and unit = "" and the title falls back to the source task's own title rather than a generated "<action> <n> <unit>" string. Target is autoTarget(12,7,1) = min(12, ceil(12/7) = 2) = 2, vary 0 so the rng is untouched.

vectors.name: two parts of one compound sharing a counter root collapse to ONE child and take NO extra sample
vectors.note: C3's children are r2 (childIndex 0, its own root) and c4 (childIndex 1, sharedCounterId r2) - the same counter family authored twice inside one compound, which counter-family exclusivity does NOT prevent (it constrains board selection, not compound authorship). r2: goal 10, monthly source to a daily board, autoTarget = min(10, ceil(10 x 1 / 30) = 1) = 1; varyRange(1, 1, 10) = [max(1, round(0.8)) = 1, min(10, round(1.2)) = 1] = [1,1], so lo == hi and the roll takes no sample. c4: goal 4, root r2, so the per-root dedupe hits BEFORE the roll and c4 takes no sample either - hence expectedRngCalls 0. Both parts resolve to the SAME derived id, so the children list collapses to one entry (first in childIndex order, keeping childIndex 0); without the collapse the compound would carry one childTaskId - and one linkId, a pure function of (compound, child) - twice.

vectors.name: the per-root dedupe is checked BEFORE the roll: a collapsed part consumes no sample
vectors.note: The discriminating twin of the vector above. There c4's own range was degenerate ([1,1]) so the sample count could not tell roll-then-dedupe from dedupe-then-roll. Here c4 carries an explicit part target 5, clamped to its goal 4, and varyRange(4, 1, 4) = [max(1, round(3.2)) = 3, min(4, round(4.8) = 5) = 4] = [3,4] - a NON-degenerate range that would consume a sample if the roll ran. It must not: c4's root is r2, which r2 (childIndex 0) already minted, so the dedupe returns that draft before rolling and expectedRngCalls stays 0. Roll-before-dedupe would make it 1 and leave the seeded sequence dependent on how many members happen to collapse. r2 itself is unchanged (auto target 1, [1,1], no sample), and the collapsed children list is the same single entry.

planDerivedTasks.idPinsNote: Literal uuidv5 outputs, computed ONCE with the TS uuidv5 (default OYBC namespace). Swift must reproduce them independently. Names: 'sources:derived:<boardId>:<root>', 'sources:derived-compound:<boardId>:<compound>', 'sources:derived-link:<derivedCompoundId>:<childId>'. The link name's <childId> is the LITERAL child task id - a derived uuid for a derived child, the raw source id for an original one. idPins itself is a clean token -> uuid map with no stray keys.
